pathway.title: Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is the binding weakness, and the trailing figure understates it. Net debt of USD 3,253.06 million at 2026-09-30 is 9.27x trailing EBITDA of USD 351.01 million and 11.61x annualised third-quarter EBITDA of USD 280.30 million. Pro forma net debt is USD 3,177.56 million (9.05x) after the Skyport Plaza sale on 2026-10-15 and USD 3,243.66 million (9.24x) after the Albuquerque studio sale on 2026-10-15, neither of which removes the sold property's earnings from EBITDA; the effect of the tender offer of 2026-10-14 is not established because the price is not stated. Trailing EBITDA holds fourth-quarter 2025 EBITDA of USD 140.57 million, USD 70.50 million above the latest quarter. The 2025 annual report attributes a USD 39.72 million increase in non-same-store office rental revenue to the Element LA early termination fee but does not size the fee or two other termination fees, which refines the statement in Financial foundation that no amount is given. Removing only that increase, as an Analyst Judgement, gives 10.45x and cash interest cover of 2.30x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M01; calculation M02; calculation M03; calculation M05; calculation M06; calculation M07; calculation M08; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 101

Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but is smaller than the headline and covers less than half of 2027 principal once the December revolver tranche lapses. Cash of USD 160.53 million, which excludes USD 44.04 million of restricted cash, plus the undrawn revolver of USD 795.25 million gives USD 955.78 million; netting USD 2.0 million of letters of credit, if they reduce availability, gives USD 953.78 million. Commitments of USD 333.3 million mature on 2026-12-21, leaving USD 462.0 million with an initial maturity of 2028-12-31 and USD 622.53 million of cash plus revolver, which is 0.42x of 2027 principal and USD 857.23 million short of it. The issuer drew USD 30.0 million on the revolver by 2026-11-06, leaving USD 765.25 million undrawn at that date; cash at that date and pro forma cash after the October tender offer and sales are not established. The minimum liquidity covenant of more than USD 125.0 million is reported as met. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M09; calculation M10; calculation M11; calculation M12; calculation M13; calculation M14; calculation M47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 29, 46–47, 73

The 2027 maturity is one refinancing event, not a ladder. Principal due in 2027 is USD 1,479.77 million, or 43.19% of contractual principal, and at 2026-09-30 99.32% of it fell due in two instruments eight days apart: the 3.95% senior notes on 2027-11-01 and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan on 2027-11-09. The loan had USD 1,069.77 million due within one year at 2025-12-31 with a maturity of 2026-08-09; it was extended by 15 months in 2026 without any paydown, USD 20.0 million was moved into a leasing reserve and excess cash flow from its properties is swept to that reserve until maturity, which traps cash at the properties. The tender offer cut the notes by USD 100.0 million, so USD 1,369.77 million now falls due in those eight days. The loan is swapped to SOFR of 3.50% plus 1.10% only to maturity: refinancing at 6.16%, the rate of the 1918 Eighth loan, or at 7.65%, which is the swap rate plus the 4.15% spread of the Office Portfolio loan, adds USD 16.69 million to USD 32.63 million of annual interest and takes annualised cover from 2.07x to between 1.85x and 1.67x. The ladder also assumes three conditional one-year extensions of the Office Portfolio loan; without them 2027 principal would be USD 1,721.85 million. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M15; calculation M16; calculation M17; calculation M18; calculation M36; calculation M43; calculation M47; calculation M20; calculation M21; calculation M19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26–28; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 99, 167

Cash generation does not fund the business, and reported free cash flow flatters it. Free cash flow was negative USD 11.74 million in nine months 2026 and negative USD 27.01 million after preferred dividends of USD 15.27 million, and the gap was met from USD 80.87 million of real estate sale proceeds and USD 15.33 million from selling Quixote equipment. Accrued but unpaid real estate investment costs rose by USD 76.19 million since 2025-12-31 and construction and executed lease commitments are USD 154.8 million, so cash capital spending will exceed the USD 83.57 million paid. Interest takes 38.51% of trailing EBITDA and 48.22% of annualised EBITDA. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M22; calculation M23; calculation M46; calculation M32; calculation M47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 46–47; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 191

Recovery prospects for unsecured holders are thinning, although the balance-sheet covenant tests still show large cushions. Secured debt rose from 41.85% of principal at 2024-12-31 to 51.01% at 2025-12-31 and 50.90% at 2026-09-30; the secured loans sit at property-owning subsidiaries and are non-recourse apart from limited customary guarantees, and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan is secured by eight properties that include the three studio lots and the Netflix-leased buildings. The issuer's own fair value puts the unsecured notes at 92.64% of par against 99.55% for secured debt, and impairments of USD 198.27 million in nine months 2026 and USD 299.32 million in FY2025 show asset values still falling. Against that, the senior note covenants report unencumbered assets at 301.5% of unsecured debt against a 150% minimum, and the ratings are unchanged at B2, B and B+ between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. Recovery is not assessed here because no executed documents or intercreditor terms are supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M26; calculation M27; calculation M37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 21, 27, 29, 35, 54–55, 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 99

Operations are improving in the assets that remain, but the earnings base is shrinking and the gain is occupancy-led. Same-store office occupancy rose 9.8 pp to 84.9% and same-store NOI rose 8.45% in the third quarter of 2026, while the average same-store rental rate fell 1.40% and total NOI fell 0.29%; revenue was 4.18% lower in nine months 2026. Leasing is capital-hungry: tenant improvements and commissions averaged USD 65.76 per square foot, roughly USD 156.62 million on the space signed. A third of office rent, 32.3%, expires in 2027 and 2028, and four tenants provide 28.6% of it, so the recovery has to repeat on rollover. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M46; calculation M38; calculation M35; calculation M25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55, 58–59, 62–63

Covenants are comfortable on balance-sheet tests and thin on coverage. The operating partnership reports compliance with every financial covenant at 2026-09-30. Fixed charge cover is the tightest test: it is reported at 1.7x against a 1.5x minimum, a gap of 0.2x or 13.33% of the minimum, after 1.6x at each of 2025-12-31, 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30. It uses an adjusted EBITDA and fixed charge definition that differs from the 2.60x cash interest cover computed here, and the filings do not reconcile the two. The asset-based tests show wider gaps, such as 15.9 pp on total liabilities to total asset value and 21.3 pp on secured indebtedness to total asset value. The minimum was printed as 1.4x at 2024-12-31 and as 1.5x since 2025-12-31, and the schedule of steps is not printed. The definitions are not printed, so covenant capacity is not calculated here. Basis: calculation M41; calculation M44; calculation M42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_hpp-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-03-31_hpp-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 171; 10-K_2024-12-31_hpp-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 170

Financial policy is creditor-aligned in action, and there is no controlling owner to extract value or to support the credit. The common dividend has not been paid in any quarter of 2025 or the first three quarters of 2026, USD 689.3 million of equity was raised in June 2025, and the Series C preferred of USD 425.0 million, which costs USD 20.19 million a year, became redeemable on 2026-11-16. Business & governance reports recourse carve-out guarantees of USD 190.5 million on three venture loans, two of which mature in 2027; this corrects the statement in Financial foundation that guarantee exposure was not established, although the issuer states the likelihood of loss as remote. The completion guarantee for Sunset Pier 94 Studios was satisfied and terminated in October 2026. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M29; calculation M28; calculation M47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 42–43, 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188

runs.text: Strengths, in order of weight. Same-store office leasing is recovering: ending occupancy rose 9.8 pp to 84.9% and same-store NOI rose 8.45%, which supports debt service in the assets that remain and shows tenants will sign in these markets. Anchor tenants are long-dated: Google, the City and County of San Francisco, Netflix and Amazon provide 28.6% of office rent on leases that run to between 2028 and 2067, which gives the rent roll visibility through the refinancing. Policy has favoured creditors: USD 689.3 million of equity was raised in June 2025, common dividends are suspended, and sales have repaid debt, so deleveraging has not been paid for by lenders. Asset-based covenants are far from their limits, which keeps default triggers on those tests distant before 2027. No principal other than small amortisation falls due before 2027, and the Hollywood loan rate is fixed by swap to its maturity, which gives a stable interest bill until then. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M25; calculation M47; calculation M41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77

Weaknesses, in order of weight. The 2027 maturities of USD 1,479.77 million are almost entirely two instruments eight days apart, and liquidity after the December 2026 revolver expiry covers 0.42x of them, so credit quality turns on one refinancing. Leverage of 9.27x to 11.61x and cash interest cover of 2.07x to 2.60x leave little room for a higher interest bill. Free cash flow is negative before preferred dividends and accrued capital costs are rising, so the business is funded by asset sales that shrink the earnings base. The secured share of debt rose to 50.90%, which puts more of the portfolio value ahead of the unsecured notes, and impairments show asset values still falling. A third of office rent expires in 2027 and 2028, rental rates in the retained assets are slipping while occupancy recovers, and the studio segment contributes 2.98% of segment profit while Quixote is wound down. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M11; calculation M13; calculation M02; calculation M04; calculation M22; calculation M23; calculation M26; calculation M37; calculation M25; calculation M40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10, 27–29, 58–59

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: In FY2025 the issuer refinanced, repaid and shrank. It obtained the Office Portfolio CMBS of USD 475.0 million in March 2025 at SOFR plus 4.15%, used the proceeds to repay USD 259.0 million drawn on the revolver and the USD 168.0 million Element LA loan, and prepaid USD 206.3 million of it after selling Element LA in the fourth quarter. It refinanced 1918 Eighth with a USD 285.0 million CMBS loan at 6.16% maturing 2030-09-11, repaid its Series B, C and D notes of USD 465.0 million, amended the revolver twice, and raised USD 689.3 million of gross equity in June 2025. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 76–77, 98, 166–167

In 2026 the issuer amended the Hollywood Media Portfolio CMBS to mature on 2027-11-09 with a swap fixing SOFR at 3.50% and a USD 20.0 million leasing reserve, sold 2001 Gateway Place and 875/899 Howard for USD 90.5 million, and drew nothing on the revolver through nine months. After the quarter end it retired USD 100.0 million each of its 2027 and 2028 senior notes by cash tender on 2026-10-14, sold Skyport Plaza and an Albuquerque studio for USD 84.9 million gross on 2026-10-15, and had USD 30.0 million drawn on the revolver at 2026-11-06. No new registered notes were issued in the period covered, and nothing after 2026-11-06 is supplied. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 47, 56, 60; calculation K14; calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial foundation for Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. (issuer hpp-1482512), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics that the five supplied filings support, in US dollars.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hudson Pacific's net leverage is 9.27x last-twelve-months EBITDA but about 11.61x on the annualised third-quarter 2026 run-rate, so creditors face the 2027 maturity wall with thinner earnings than the trailing figure suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The trailing figure includes fourth-quarter 2025 EBITDA of USD 140.57 million, about twice a 2026 quarter, which the Element LA lease termination fee tied to its sale probably lifted. Net leverage fell from 13.55x at the end of FY2024 mainly because debt was repaid from the June 2025 equity raise and property sales rather than from EBITDA growth; cash interest cover is 2.60x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C31; calculation C35; calculation C13; calculation C29; calculation C34

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net leverage on reported EBITDA fell from 13.55x at the end of FY2024 to 9.92x at the end of FY2025 and 9.27x on the trailing basis at 2026-09-30. Total debt at carrying value, joint venture partner debt included, fell from USD 4,242.98 million to USD 3,417.59 million in FY2025, a fall of USD 825.39 million, and was USD 3,413.60 million at 2026-09-30. The FY2025 repayment came from the equity raise and sales, not from earnings: net debt repayment was USD 719.22 million against net equity proceeds of USD 661.84 million, and EBITDA rose only from USD 308.55 million to USD 330.41 million. Debt carrying value barely moved in 2026, so further deleveraging has to come from earnings or sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C29; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C70; calculation C61; calculation C62; calculation C71; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 98, 124–125, 128–129

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fourth-quarter 2025 EBITDA of USD 140.57 million, derived as FY2025 less nine months 2025, compares with USD 67.75 million, USD 72.62 million and USD 70.07 million in the first three quarters of 2026, an excess of USD 70.50 million over the latest quarter. The filing says termination fee income was received at Element LA in connection with its sale in the fourth quarter of 2025 and cites other termination fees, but states none of the amounts, so the quarter's excess cannot be sized exactly. Annualising the third quarter gives EBITDA of USD 280.30 million, net leverage of 11.61x and cash interest cover of 2.07x, which is the better guide to the run-rate that creditors are actually lending against. EBITDA is calculated from the statements because the issuer states none.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C13; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C72; calculation C15; calculation C35; calculation C36; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 76, 93, 101

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash interest paid, net of capitalized interest, fell from USD 170.98 million in FY2024 to USD 164.02 million in FY2025 and USD 135.17 million on the trailing basis, so cover rose from 1.80x to 2.01x and 2.60x. Cash interest paid fell by USD 28.86 million between nine months 2025 and nine months 2026, more than the USD 22.04 million fall in gross interest expense, so part of the cash saving may be timing, and capitalized interest fell by USD 13.04 million as development projects were completed, which pushes more interest into expense. The issuer's own covenant cover, adjusted EBITDA to fixed charges, is 1.7x against a minimum of 1.5x, on a definition the filings do not print.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C32; calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C73; calculation C74; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–30, 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Impairment charges were USD 149.66 million in FY2024, USD 299.32 million in FY2025 and USD 198.27 million in nine months 2026, including USD 147.83 million in the third quarter on the Hill7 and Skyport Plaza office properties after their expected holding periods were shortened. They sit below the operating line, so EBITDA does not fall, but they show asset values dropping: total equity fell by USD 382.09 million from the end of FY2025 to 2026-09-30, and a net-loss-based EBITDA would be negative USD 45.39 million for FY2025, which would make leverage meaningless.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C69; calculation C58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 125

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow of USD 77.65 million in nine months 2026 did not cover additions to real estate of USD 83.57 million and to other property of USD 5.81 million, so free cash flow was negative USD 11.74 million before preferred dividends of USD 15.27 million, and negative USD 27.01 million after them. Cash still rose from USD 138.36 million to USD 160.53 million, helped by USD 80.87 million of real estate sale proceeds and USD 15.33 million from selling equipment as parts of the Quixote production services business are wound down. In nine months 2026 the company funded its capital spending and preferred dividends from asset sales rather than from operations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C45; calculation C47; calculation C68; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11, 75

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer's own fair value estimate, a model value on prevailing rates for similar instruments rather than a quote, puts the unsecured notes at USD 1,528.54 million against principal of USD 1,650.00 million, or 92.64% of par, and secured debt at 99.55% of principal, so the unsecured creditors carry the discount. The 2027 maturities are USD 1,479.77 million, or 43.19% of contractual principal of USD 3,426.49 million, made up of the 3.95% notes due 2027 and the Hollywood Media Portfolio CMBS. Revolver commitments of USD 333.3 million mature on 2026-12-21, so the undrawn USD 795.25 million shown at 2026-09-30 falls to USD 462.0 million before any new borrowing; at 2026-11-06 USD 30.0 million was drawn. After the balance-sheet date the issuer repurchased USD 100.0 million each of the 2027 and 2028 notes on 2026-10-14 with cash and revolver borrowing, at a price the filing does not state, and sold two properties on 2026-10-15 for USD 84.90 million gross, which would lower net debt of USD 3,253.06 million to USD 3,168.16 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C48; calculation C51; calculation C56; calculation C40; calculation C77; calculation C78; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 35, 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case that credit quality is improving is that EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026 of USD 70.07 million was 1.63% above the third quarter of 2025, nothing was drawn on the revolver through nine months 2026, and the operating partnership reports compliance with every financial covenant. Occupied in-service office space was 85.6% at 2026-09-30 against 76.3% at 2025-12-31, but the in-service office perimeter fell from 39 to 35 properties as properties were sold or moved to repositioning and held for sale, so that rise is not like for like. Revenue is still falling: it was 4.18% lower in nine months 2026 than a year earlier.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation C60; calculation C63; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28–29, 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if quarterly EBITDA stayed above USD 70.07 million while the 2026-12-21 revolver tranche is extended or replaced and the 2027 maturities are refinanced without a rise in cash interest. It would worsen if EBITDA reverts toward the pre-termination level, if the December 2026 tranche is not replaced, or if the 3.95% notes and the Hollywood Media Portfolio CMBS due in 2027 meet a closed refinancing market for office-weighted collateral. The Hill7 CMBS also starts to accrue a further 2.00% a year, added to principal, from 2026-11-06.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every leverage and cover figure rests on EBITDA calculated from the statements as revenue less operating expenses plus depreciation and amortization, because the issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA. Interim statements are unaudited, the fourth quarter of 2025 is derived as the year less nine months, and the termination fee income inside it is not quantified in the filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The executed credit agreement and indentures are not supplied, so covenant definitions, the rank and guarantee terms of each instrument and any intercreditor terms are taken from the filing summaries. Debt held by unconsolidated ventures, letters of credit and the use of the October 2026 sale proceeds are outside the debt figures, and no filing after 2026-11-06 is available.

fields.value: The ratios use calculated EBITDA, and the trailing and FY2025 figures include fourth-quarter 2025 termination income, so run-rate leverage is higher.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: Subsequent events after the balance-sheet date of 2026-09-30, each kept out of period figures: on 2026-10-14 the company repurchased USD 100.0 million of its 3.95% senior notes due 2027 and USD 100.0 million of its 5.95% senior notes due 2028 by cash tender offer; on 2026-10-15 it sold Skyport Plaza for USD 75.5 million gross and an Albuquerque studio for USD 9.4 million gross; on 2026-10-28 Weil, Gotshal & Manges announced a wind-down, and its remaining lease of 50,829 square feet runs to 2038; on 2026-11-06 USD 30.0 million was drawn on the revolver; from 2026-11-06 the Hill7 CMBS accrues an extra 2.00% a year added to principal; on 2026-12-21 USD 333.3 million of revolver commitments mature.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA and no adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is calculated from the statements as revenue less operating expenses plus depreciation and amortization, and no adjusted ratio or EBITDA bridge is stated. Every leverage and cover figure is restricted to that definition. This is a Medium severity gap that an issuer EBITDA reconciliation in an earnings release or lender presentation would close.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The amounts of lease termination fee income in FY2025 are not stated: the Element LA fee was received in connection with its sale in the fourth quarter, and the fees at 6040 Sunset and Fourth and Traction have no stated quarter, so trailing EBITDA of USD 351.01 million and FY2025 interest cover cannot be normalised exactly. This is a High severity gap because the same inputs give net leverage of 9.27x on the trailing basis and 11.61x on the annualised third quarter; the fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release would close it.

The revolver draw is known only to 2026-11-06, at USD 30.0 million. This is a Medium severity gap closed by the offer documents or any filing after 2026-11-06.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Debt of unconsolidated ventures is outside Total Debt: the Bentall Centre loan of USD 466.123 million drawn (HPP owns 20.0%, matures 2027-07-01), the Sunset Glenoaks Studios loan of USD 107.833 million (50.0%, matures 2027-01-09) and the Sunset Pier 94 Studios loan of USD 169.771 million (25.6%, matures 2028-09-09), as printed. Whether the company guarantees any of it is not established beyond a USD 2.0 million letter of credit for the Pier 94 completion guarantee. This is a Medium severity gap closed by the venture loan agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The security and rank of the joint venture partner debt of USD 66.136 million are not stated, so it is left out of the debt stack, although it is in Total Debt and in the maturity ladder. This is a Low severity gap closed by the Ferry Building venture documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Letters of credit of USD 2.0 million under the revolver and USD 3.1 million for tenant improvements at the Office Portfolio CMBS properties are not netted from undrawn capacity, because the filing shows remaining capacity without netting them and does not say whether they reduce availability. This is a Low severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Lines the filings print as a dash are carried as not supplied rather than zero, and lines that exist in one period's statement only are marked as not in the other statements. The filings' own totals treat the dashes as nil, so this restricts nothing numerically. This is a Low severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The FY2023 statements, the 2025 quarterly columns other than the third, the first-quarter and first-half 2026 cash flow statements and the separate statements of the operating partnership are not extracted. The balance sheet, cash flow and cash roll-forward identities hold in every extracted column. This is a Low severity gap closed by extending the extraction.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The Hill7 CMBS accrues a further 2.00% a year, added to principal, from 2026-11-06, so the contractual principal for 2028 will exceed USD 101.00 million; the filing does not state the amount. This is a Low severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Per-share amounts use weighted average shares that include pre-funded warrants, 64,491,988 for the third quarter of 2026 against 54,277,747 shares outstanding at 2026-09-30, so they are not per share outstanding; FY2024 per-share amounts are restated for the one-for-seven reverse split. This is a Low severity gap.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and transaction fact pack for Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. (issuer hpp-1482512), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, ownership, operating model, transactions and governance and sponsor behaviour that the five supplied filings support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hudson Pacific is a widely held Class-A office and studio landlord with no controlling owner identified in the filings, so unsecured creditors depend on leasing recovery and asset sales, not on owner support, to meet near-term maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Office space was 85.6% occupied at 2026-09-30 on a smaller in-service portfolio, 32.3% of office annualized base rent expires in 2027 and 2028, and four tenants provide 28.6% of it. Management has suspended common dividends, raised equity in 2025 and sold properties to retire debt, which is creditor-aligned, but the filings give no board or shareholder detail beyond signatures and cover pages.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K09; calculation K08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 54, 58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Control appears dispersed, which removes sponsor extraction risk and also any sponsor backstop. The charter caps any holder at 9.8% of the shares unless the board exempts it, 75 holders of record were reported in February 2026, and the company owns about 96.7% of the operating partnership that issues the debt, the rest being held by executives, directors and affiliates. Creditors therefore cannot count on an equity cure from an owner; the equity cushion is the market value of the stock and the USD 425.0 million Series C preferred, which ranks ahead of the common and became redeemable by the company on 2026-11-16. Total debt was 73.8% of total market capitalization at 2026-09-30.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K21; calculation K23; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 42, 74

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leasing risk is concentrated in a few years and a few tenants. Office annualized base rent is USD 460,366,732 on HPP's share, of which 12.4% expires in 2027 and 19.9% in 2028, including the Google expirations in 2028 and 2029, and the four largest tenants provide 28.6%. Vacancy at 2026-09-30 included most of Skyport Plaza, which was sold on 2026-10-15. The announced wind-down of Weil, Gotshal & Manges on 2026-10-28 puts a lease running to 2038, about 0.8% of rent on the company's basis, at risk of non-payment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K09; calculation K08; calculation K20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47, 54–55, 58–59

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The operating model is an office business with a small, volatile studio segment. Office provided 81.74% of revenue and studio 18.26% in nine months 2026, but studio provided only 2.98% of segment profit, and the studio segment lost money in FY2025. Same-store office occupancy rose by 9.8 percentage points to 84.9% between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026 and same-store NOI rose 8.45%, so the recovery is real where it is measured, while total NOI fell 0.3% because asset sales and the expiry of the PayPal lease at Fourth and Traction removed income.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K01; calculation K02; calculation K07; calculation K18; calculation K19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45, 62–63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation is creditor-aligned on the evidence but has shifted risk toward unsecured holders. The company suspended common dividends, raised gross equity proceeds of USD 689.3 million in June 2025, sold properties for USD 247.0 million in FY2025 and USD 90.5 million in nine months 2026, and paid down debt. Over the same period it repaid unsecured Series B, C and D notes of USD 465.0 million and raised CMBS loans on the Office Portfolio and 1918 Eighth properties, so secured debt rose from 41.85% of unsecured and secured principal at 2024-12-31 to 51.01% at 2025-12-31 and 50.90% at 2026-09-30, which narrows the unencumbered pool behind the unsecured notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K10; calculation K11; calculation K12; calculation K13; calculation K14; calculation K26; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 76–77, 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 26, 41, 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Contingent exposure sits in the joint ventures. The company has given recourse carve-out guarantees of USD 190.5 million on three unconsolidated venture loans and states the likelihood of loss as remote, but the Bentall Centre and Sunset Glenoaks Studios loans mature in 2027 and the Sunset Pier 94 Studios loan in 2028, so ventures that cannot refinance will test partner and lender support. The completion guarantee for Sunset Pier 94 Studios was terminated in October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the same-store recovery and leasing volume: the company leased 39.78% more square feet in nine months 2026 than a year earlier, same-store office occupancy and NOI rose, general and administrative expense fell 38.44% and the operating partnership reports no event of default. No controlling owner or sponsor has extracted value, and the company has used equity and sales, not creditors, to fund deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation K17; calculation K18; calculation K19; calculation K22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 59, 62–63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That view would win if same-store gains persist while the 2027 and 2028 expiries roll at current rents, the December 2026 revolver tranche is replaced and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan is refinanced in 2027. It would lose if the Google, Weil or other large expiries are not backfilled, if sales continue to shrink the portfolio faster than leasing improves it, or if a venture loan cannot be refinanced and the guarantees are called.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement, which holds board composition, committee structure, executive pay and beneficial owners above the operating partnership, is not supplied, so the conclusion that control is dispersed rests on the 9.8% charter cap and the record-holder count and could change if a holder above that level has been exempted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No document dated after 2026-11-06 is supplied, so the conclusion that the October 2026 tender, sales and the Weil announcement are the latest events could change if a later filing reports further transactions.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The executed joint venture agreements and loan documents are not supplied, so the size of the guarantee exposure is taken from the quarterly report's stated amounts and could be higher if other support obligations exist.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In FY2025 the issuer refinanced, repaid and shrank. It obtained the Office Portfolio CMBS of USD 475.0 million in March 2025 at SOFR plus 4.15%, used the proceeds to repay USD 259.0 million drawn on the revolver and the USD 168.0 million Element LA loan, and prepaid USD 206.3 million of it after selling Element LA in the fourth quarter. It refinanced 1918 Eighth with a USD 285.0 million CMBS loan at 6.16% maturing 2030-09-11, repaid its Series B, C and D notes of USD 465.0 million, amended the revolver twice, and raised USD 689.3 million of gross equity in June 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In 2026 the issuer amended the Hollywood Media Portfolio CMBS to mature on 2027-11-09 with a swap fixing SOFR at 3.50% and a USD 20.0 million leasing reserve, sold 2001 Gateway Place and 875/899 Howard for USD 90.5 million, and drew nothing on the revolver through nine months. After the quarter end it retired USD 100.0 million each of its 2027 and 2028 senior notes by cash tender on 2026-10-14, sold Skyport Plaza and an Albuquerque studio for USD 84.9 million gross on 2026-10-15, and had USD 30.0 million drawn on the revolver at 2026-11-06. No new registered notes were issued in the period covered, and nothing after 2026-11-06 is supplied.

fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28, 47, 56, 60; calculation K14; calculation K15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Medium. The risk level is driven by the absence of a sponsor and incomplete governance disclosure and by a rising secured share of debt, because unsecured creditors sit behind more secured claims and cannot count on owner support, which implies a monitoring posture. Countervailing evidence is the creditor-aligned financial policy of equity raising, dividend suspension and asset sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement, which carries board composition, committees, executive pay and beneficial owners, is not supplied, so the control and board findings rest on the charter cap, record-holder count and signature pages. This is a Medium severity gap closed by the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The price paid in the 2026-10-14 tender offer and the net proceeds of the 2026-10-15 sales are not stated, so the effect on remaining creditors is not established. This is a Medium severity gap closed by the offer documents or a later filing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Executed credit agreement, indentures and venture loan agreements are not supplied, so the legal-capacity link of every behavior flag is not established. This is a Medium severity gap closed by the executed documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The names of the partners in the consolidated Hollywood studios venture and the unconsolidated ventures are not stated, apart from PIMCO, so partner alignment is not established. This is a Low severity gap.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote

fields.value: | 1 | 2027 maturity concentration | USD 1,479.767 million of principal falls due in 2027, 43.19% of 3,426.486; USD 1,469.767 million of it on 2027-11-01 and 2027-11-09. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–28; calculation M15; calculation M16 | Two instruments need refinancing within eight days, and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan was extended in 2026 by 15 months without paydown. | The refinancing outcome decides default risk on the unsecured notes; liquidity covers 0.65x of 2027 principal before the December expiry. | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 2 | Revolver expiry and liquidity coverage | USD 333.3 million of commitments mature on 2026-12-21; cash plus revolver falls from 955.783 to 622.533. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 73; calculation M09; calculation M11 | Undrawn capacity shrinks before the 2027 refinancing and the October tender offer and USD 30.0 million draw have already used some of it. | Liquidity covers 0.42x of 2027 principal after the expiry, so the runway depends on operating cash flow and sales. | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 3 | Leverage and EBITDA quality | Net leverage 9.27x trailing and 11.61x on annualised Q3 2026; Q4 2025 EBITDA 140.570 against 70.074. 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 93, 101; calculation M02; calculation M03 | Trailing EBITDA includes termination income that leaves the window at 2026-12-31. | Reported leverage will rise toward 11.6x and lenders will underwrite the refinancing on run-rate EBITDA. | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 4 | Cash flow after capital and preferred dividends | Free cash flow -11.736 and -27.009 in nine months 2026; accrued real estate payables up 76.193; commitments 154.8. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 46–47; calculation M22; calculation M23 | Operating cash flow does not cover leasing, capital spending and preferred dividends, so asset sales fund the gap. | Deleveraging depends on disposals, and internal cash does not contribute to the 2027 maturities. | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 5 | Refinancing cost | Hollywood loan all-in 4.60% to maturity against 6.16% and 7.65% references; added interest 16.688 to 32.628. calculation M20; calculation M21 | The swap protection ends at maturity, and the reference rates are other loans, not quotes. | Run-rate cash interest cover would fall to between 1.85x and 1.67x, and fixed charge cover of 1.7x against 1.5x would tighten. | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 6 | Rising secured share and falling asset values | Secured share 41.85% to 50.90%; unsecured notes at 92.64% of par; impairments 198.265 in nine months 2026. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 21, 35; calculation M26; calculation M27 | Property-level non-recourse CMBS ranks ahead of the unsecured notes on pledged properties, and impairments lower asset coverage. | Unsecured recovery prospects are thinner; senior note asset coverage fell from 316.8% to 301.5% in the third quarter. | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 7 | Tenant rollover and concentration | 32.3% of office rent expires in 2027 and 2028; four tenants provide 28.6%; Weil announced a wind-down on 2026-10-28. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47, 54–55, 58; calculation M25 | Large tenants hold bargaining power and expiries cluster ahead of the maturities. | Backfill risk falls on the cash flows that support the refinancing. | Negative | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 8 | Earnings base lost to asset sales | Total NOI -0.29% in Q3 2026 against same-store +8.45%; non-same-store NOI -4.003 against +2.974. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; calculation M46; calculation M24 | Sales and expiries remove income faster than same-store leasing adds it. | Each sale lowers debt but also EBITDA, so net leverage falls less than debt does. | Negative | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 9 | Same-store leasing recovery | Same-store office occupancy up 9.8 pp to 84.9%; same-store NOI up 8.45%. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 62–63; calculation M24 | Retained assets produce more NOI as space is let. | Supports debt service and the collateral for the refinancing, although the gain is occupancy-led and rent per square foot fell 1.40%. | Positive | High |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: | 10 | Asset sales used for debt reduction | Sales of USD 90.5 million in nine months 2026 and USD 84.9 million after quarter end; pro forma net debt 3,177.564 after the Skyport sale. 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47, 56; calculation M05; calculation M47 | Proceeds retire unsecured notes and cash tender at a price not stated. | Lowers principal and interest and shows a disposal market for non-strategic assets. | Positive | Medium |

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. (issuer hpp-1482512), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the business, financial profile, liquidity and refinancing position of the registrant, whose operating partnership, Hudson Pacific Properties, L.P., issues the debt, as the five supplied filings and the three accepted analyst modules support it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hudson Pacific is a weak, highly leveraged office and studio landlord whose liquidity does not cover its 2027 maturities, so unsecured noteholders depend on refinancing the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan and the 2027 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash plus the undrawn revolver of USD 955.78 million at 2026-09-30 covers 0.65x of the USD 1,479.77 million of principal due in 2027, and 0.42x once USD 333.3 million of revolver commitments mature on 2026-12-21. That is before the October 2026 tender offer, whose cash cost is not established, and the USD 30.0 million revolver draw reported at 2026-11-06. Cash interest cover is 2.60x on trailing EBITDA but 2.07x on annualised third-quarter EBITDA over trailing cash interest, because fourth-quarter 2025 carried lease termination income. Same-store office leasing is recovering and every covenant is reported as met, which supports the next twelve months but does not retire the 2027 wall.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M09; calculation M13; calculation M04; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 47, 73

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is the binding weakness, and the trailing figure understates it. Net debt of USD 3,253.06 million at 2026-09-30 is 9.27x trailing EBITDA of USD 351.01 million and 11.61x annualised third-quarter EBITDA of USD 280.30 million. Pro forma net debt is USD 3,177.56 million (9.05x) after the Skyport Plaza sale on 2026-10-15 and USD 3,243.66 million (9.24x) after the Albuquerque studio sale on 2026-10-15, neither of which removes the sold property's earnings from EBITDA; the effect of the tender offer of 2026-10-14 is not established because the price is not stated. Trailing EBITDA holds fourth-quarter 2025 EBITDA of USD 140.57 million, USD 70.50 million above the latest quarter. The 2025 annual report attributes a USD 39.72 million increase in non-same-store office rental revenue to the Element LA early termination fee but does not size the fee or two other termination fees, which refines the statement in Financial foundation that no amount is given. Removing only that increase, as an Analyst Judgement, gives 10.45x and cash interest cover of 2.30x.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months but is smaller than the headline and covers less than half of 2027 principal once the December revolver tranche lapses. Cash of USD 160.53 million, which excludes USD 44.04 million of restricted cash, plus the undrawn revolver of USD 795.25 million gives USD 955.78 million; netting USD 2.0 million of letters of credit, if they reduce availability, gives USD 953.78 million. Commitments of USD 333.3 million mature on 2026-12-21, leaving USD 462.0 million with an initial maturity of 2028-12-31 and USD 622.53 million of cash plus revolver, which is 0.42x of 2027 principal and USD 857.23 million short of it. The issuer drew USD 30.0 million on the revolver by 2026-11-06, leaving USD 765.25 million undrawn at that date; cash at that date and pro forma cash after the October tender offer and sales are not established. The minimum liquidity covenant of more than USD 125.0 million is reported as met.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 2027 maturity is one refinancing event, not a ladder. Principal due in 2027 is USD 1,479.77 million, or 43.19% of contractual principal, and at 2026-09-30 99.32% of it fell due in two instruments eight days apart: the 3.95% senior notes on 2027-11-01 and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan on 2027-11-09. The loan had USD 1,069.77 million due within one year at 2025-12-31 with a maturity of 2026-08-09; it was extended by 15 months in 2026 without any paydown, USD 20.0 million was moved into a leasing reserve and excess cash flow from its properties is swept to that reserve until maturity, which traps cash at the properties. The tender offer cut the notes by USD 100.0 million, so USD 1,369.77 million now falls due in those eight days. The loan is swapped to SOFR of 3.50% plus 1.10% only to maturity: refinancing at 6.16%, the rate of the 1918 Eighth loan, or at 7.65%, which is the swap rate plus the 4.15% spread of the Office Portfolio loan, adds USD 16.69 million to USD 32.63 million of annual interest and takes annualised cover from 2.07x to between 1.85x and 1.67x. The ladder also assumes three conditional one-year extensions of the Office Portfolio loan; without them 2027 principal would be USD 1,721.85 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation does not fund the business, and reported free cash flow flatters it. Free cash flow was negative USD 11.74 million in nine months 2026 and negative USD 27.01 million after preferred dividends of USD 15.27 million, and the gap was met from USD 80.87 million of real estate sale proceeds and USD 15.33 million from selling Quixote equipment. Accrued but unpaid real estate investment costs rose by USD 76.19 million since 2025-12-31 and construction and executed lease commitments are USD 154.8 million, so cash capital spending will exceed the USD 83.57 million paid. Interest takes 38.51% of trailing EBITDA and 48.22% of annualised EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Recovery prospects for unsecured holders are thinning, although the balance-sheet covenant tests still show large cushions. Secured debt rose from 41.85% of principal at 2024-12-31 to 51.01% at 2025-12-31 and 50.90% at 2026-09-30; the secured loans sit at property-owning subsidiaries and are non-recourse apart from limited customary guarantees, and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan is secured by eight properties that include the three studio lots and the Netflix-leased buildings. The issuer's own fair value puts the unsecured notes at 92.64% of par against 99.55% for secured debt, and impairments of USD 198.27 million in nine months 2026 and USD 299.32 million in FY2025 show asset values still falling. Against that, the senior note covenants report unencumbered assets at 301.5% of unsecured debt against a 150% minimum, and the ratings are unchanged at B2, B and B+ between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. Recovery is not assessed here because no executed documents or intercreditor terms are supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operations are improving in the assets that remain, but the earnings base is shrinking and the gain is occupancy-led. Same-store office occupancy rose 9.8 pp to 84.9% and same-store NOI rose 8.45% in the third quarter of 2026, while the average same-store rental rate fell 1.40% and total NOI fell 0.29%; revenue was 4.18% lower in nine months 2026. Leasing is capital-hungry: tenant improvements and commissions averaged USD 65.76 per square foot, roughly USD 156.62 million on the space signed. A third of office rent, 32.3%, expires in 2027 and 2028, and four tenants provide 28.6% of it, so the recovery has to repeat on rollover.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M46; calculation M38; calculation M35; calculation M25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 54–55, 58–59, 62–63

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenants are comfortable on balance-sheet tests and thin on coverage. The operating partnership reports compliance with every financial covenant at 2026-09-30. Fixed charge cover is the tightest test: it is reported at 1.7x against a 1.5x minimum, a gap of 0.2x or 13.33% of the minimum, after 1.6x at each of 2025-12-31, 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30. It uses an adjusted EBITDA and fixed charge definition that differs from the 2.60x cash interest cover computed here, and the filings do not reconcile the two. The asset-based tests show wider gaps, such as 15.9 pp on total liabilities to total asset value and 21.3 pp on secured indebtedness to total asset value. The minimum was printed as 1.4x at 2024-12-31 and as 1.5x since 2025-12-31, and the schedule of steps is not printed. The definitions are not printed, so covenant capacity is not calculated here.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M41; calculation M44; calculation M42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; 10-Q_2026-06-30_hpp-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-Q_2026-03-31_hpp-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 171; 10-K_2024-12-31_hpp-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 170

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is creditor-aligned in action, and there is no controlling owner to extract value or to support the credit. The common dividend has not been paid in any quarter of 2025 or the first three quarters of 2026, USD 689.3 million of equity was raised in June 2025, and the Series C preferred of USD 425.0 million, which costs USD 20.19 million a year, became redeemable on 2026-11-16. Business & governance reports recourse carve-out guarantees of USD 190.5 million on three venture loans, two of which mature in 2027; this corrects the statement in Financial foundation that guarantee exposure was not established, although the issuer states the likelihood of loss as remote. The completion guarantee for Sunset Pier 94 Studios was satisfied and terminated in October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M29; calculation M28; calculation M47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 23, 42–43, 75; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 188

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against the weak view is that the 2027 wall is two refinancings with large asset cover behind them. Unencumbered assets are 301.5% of unsecured debt against a 150% minimum, secured debt is 21.4% of total assets against a 40% maximum, same-store NOI is growing at 8.45%, the revolver was undrawn through September 2026, equity markets were open in June 2025, and ratings were unchanged between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30. The Hollywood Media Portfolio loan is secured by eight properties that include buildings leased to Netflix to 2031, the company extended it in 2026 without a paydown, and the October 2026 sales and tender offer show disposals being turned into debt reduction. Equity capitalization of USD 1,195.54 million, including the Series C preferred, sits beneath USD 3,363.15 million of debt, which is 73.8% of total market capitalization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 29, 54–55, 74

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan and the 3.95% notes are refinanced early at an all-in cost near 6.16% rather than 7.65%, the December 2026 revolver tranche is replaced, and quarterly EBITDA holds above USD 70.07 million without termination income. It would worsen if refinancing prices near the Office Portfolio spread, which adds USD 32.63 million of annual interest and cuts annualised cover to 1.67x, if the Office Portfolio extensions are not met, if tenants fail as Weil, Gotshal & Manges announced a wind-down on 2026-10-28, if disposals stop before leverage falls, or if fixed charge cover moves toward its 1.5x minimum.

fields.value: - Covenant definitions are not printed and the ratios are rounded to one decimal, so the conclusion that fixed charge cover is the tightest test cannot be verified and could change with the executed terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No sector data, tenant credit reports or market rent evidence is supplied, so the conclusions on rollover risk and on the studio segment rest on the issuer's own descriptions and could be better or worse than the filings suggest.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths, in order of weight. Same-store office leasing is recovering: ending occupancy rose 9.8 pp to 84.9% and same-store NOI rose 8.45%, which supports debt service in the assets that remain and shows tenants will sign in these markets. Anchor tenants are long-dated: Google, the City and County of San Francisco, Netflix and Amazon provide 28.6% of office rent on leases that run to between 2028 and 2067, which gives the rent roll visibility through the refinancing. Policy has favoured creditors: USD 689.3 million of equity was raised in June 2025, common dividends are suspended, and sales have repaid debt, so deleveraging has not been paid for by lenders. Asset-based covenants are far from their limits, which keeps default triggers on those tests distant before 2027. No principal other than small amortisation falls due before 2027, and the Hollywood loan rate is fixed by swap to its maturity, which gives a stable interest bill until then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M25; calculation M47; calculation M41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses, in order of weight. The 2027 maturities of USD 1,479.77 million are almost entirely two instruments eight days apart, and liquidity after the December 2026 revolver expiry covers 0.42x of them, so credit quality turns on one refinancing. Leverage of 9.27x to 11.61x and cash interest cover of 2.07x to 2.60x leave little room for a higher interest bill. Free cash flow is negative before preferred dividends and accrued capital costs are rising, so the business is funded by asset sales that shrink the earnings base. The secured share of debt rose to 50.90%, which puts more of the portfolio value ahead of the unsecured notes, and impairments show asset values still falling. A third of office rent expires in 2027 and 2028, rental rates in the retained assets are slipping while occupancy recovers, and the studio segment contributes 2.98% of segment profit while Quixote is wound down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M11; calculation M13; calculation M02; calculation M04; calculation M22; calculation M23; calculation M26; calculation M37; calculation M25; calculation M40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 10, 27–29, 58–59

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Module status: Full Run. The five filings cover the period from FY2024 to 2026-09-30 and every gating input for a fundamental synthesis: statements, debt note, covenants, liquidity, commitments, leasing and subsequent events to 2026-11-06. Datapoints taken from the earlier modules, all for the run as of 2026-11-18 and the period to 2026-09-30, are net debt, EBITDA, leverage, cover, free cash flow and the pro forma rows from Financial foundation; occupancy, expiries, tenants, secured share and guarantees from Business & governance; and the cutoff gap after 2026-11-06 from Source readiness. Executed credit documents, market data, peer data and agency reports are not supplied and are treated as limitations, not as blocks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 82

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. is a Maryland real estate investment trust headquartered in Los Angeles that owns, leases, develops and operates Class-A office and studio properties in Los Angeles, the San Francisco Bay Area, Seattle, New York and Vancouver, with a studio development in Greater London. At 2026-09-30 the portfolio held 51 properties: 38 consolidated office properties, three consolidated studio properties and five consolidated development sites, plus five properties and sites held through unconsolidated ventures. Office space was 85.6% occupied on a perimeter of 35 in-service properties after sales and repositioning. Office provided 81.74% of revenue and studio 18.26% in nine months 2026, but studio provided only 2.98% of segment profit, and Quixote, the production services business, is being wound down after operating losses in 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 22, 34, 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 36

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The model supports cash-flow visibility through contractual rent from long-dated anchor leases, which supports debt service on the retained portfolio. It weakens refinancing confidence because the rent is concentrated in technology and media tenants and in California and the Pacific Northwest, because each sale removes income, and because the studio and production services lines move with production activity. Liquidity is preserved by suspending the common dividend and cutting overhead, not by growth in cash generation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: There is no controlling owner, which removes sponsor extraction risk and also any sponsor backstop. The charter caps any holder at 9.8% of shares unless the board exempts it, 75 holders of record were reported on 2026-02-18, and the board alone sets investment and financing policy, with no limit on debt in the organizational documents and the power to change the borrowing policy without a stockholder vote. Creditors therefore rely on covenants rather than on policy statements, and the management aim of conservative leverage is not a binding limit while debt is 73.8% of total market capitalization.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. is the sole general partner of Hudson Pacific Properties, L.P. and owns about 96.7% of it including unvested units. The operating partnership issues the unsecured notes and borrows under the revolver, and Hudson Pacific Properties, Inc. and certain subsidiaries guarantee its unsecured debt; the secured loans sit in separate property-owning subsidiaries that are not obligors of other debt, so unsecured holders rank behind secured lenders on the pledged properties. The equity beneath the debt is USD 770.54 million of implied common equity at the 2026-09-30 closing price and the USD 425.0 million Series C preferred, which ranks ahead of the common, costs USD 20.19 million a year and became redeemable by the company on 2026-11-16, so a redemption would use cash that supports debt service. The Ferry Building venture is 55.0% owned with PIMCO, which holds put rights and is owed USD 66.14 million that sits in consolidated debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M31; calculation M29; calculation M47; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 48, 70, 171; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 29, 42, 74

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is mostly recurring, contractual office rent, and it is falling with a smaller portfolio. Office rental revenue was USD 439.57 million of USD 551.04 million of total revenue in nine months 2026, total revenue fell 4.18%, and studio service revenue of USD 60.86 million is volatile because it depends on production activity. The recovery is led by occupancy, not price: same-store ending occupancy rose 9.8 pp while the average annual rental rate per square foot fell to USD 56.28 from USD 57.08, and the company states that its office rents are generally below current market quotes without giving the quotes. The portfolio's in-place rent is USD 54.23 per square foot and rises contractually to USD 62.65 at expiry; that is a scheduled rent, not a market rent, so it does not show rollover upside, which corrects the reading in Business & governance. The 2028 expiries are in place at USD 71.11 per square foot, the highest of any expiry year and well above the portfolio average, so renewals that year are the most exposed to any gap between in-place and market rent, which the filings do not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M53; calculation M38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 58–59, 62; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 77

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration and cyclicality set the revenue risk. Four tenants provide 28.6% of office rent, 32.3% expires in 2027 and 2028 and 58.4% between 2028 and 2031, and Weil, Gotshal & Manges announced a wind-down on 2026-10-28 with a lease to 2038 that is about 0.8% of rent on the company's basis and 0.9% on the overview basis, a difference the filing does not reconcile. Revenue is predictable where leases are long and anchored, cyclical where it depends on technology and media demand, discretionary in the studio lines, and declining in total because of sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M25; calculation M50; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47, 54–55, 58–59; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are defended by cost cuts and sales, not by pricing, and they have little room to absorb a revenue fall. EBITDA margin was 38.74% in the third quarter of 2026 against 36.95% a year earlier, but over nine months office revenue fell 5.30% while office operating expense fell only 2.29%, which is operating deleverage in a largely fixed property cost base. Studio operating expense fell 15.15% against revenue growth of 1.19% as Quixote was cut back. General and administrative expense fell 38.44%, but USD 14.3 million of the 2025 base was accelerated compensation that does not recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M33; calculation M34; calculation M48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 72

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest is the largest fixed charge: cash interest takes 38.51% of trailing EBITDA and 48.22% of annualised EBITDA, so a revenue shortfall or a higher refinancing rate passes straight to coverage. Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure by further cost cutting, but not against a combination of lease expiries and a higher interest bill.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA converts to little free cash flow because leasing and capital costs are heavy and interest absorbs about two-fifths of it. Free cash flow was negative USD 11.74 million in nine months 2026 on EBITDA of USD 210.44 million, and the filing gives no split between maintenance and growth capital. Leasing is the main call: tenant improvements and commissions averaged USD 65.76 per square foot on leases signed in nine months 2026 and USD 99.76 on new leases against USD 86.10 a year earlier, and construction and executed lease commitments are USD 154.8 million against USD 96.7 million at 2025-12-31. Accrued payables for real estate investments of USD 196.20 million are USD 76.19 million higher than at 2025-12-31, so cash capital spending is running ahead of the reported USD 83.57 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M22; calculation M23; calculation M35; calculation M47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10, 46–47, 59; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 100, 191

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capex flexibility is limited near term by those commitments and by Washington 1000, a 546,000 square foot building placed in service in 2026 with stabilisation estimated for the fourth quarter of 2027. The future development pipeline has no committed completion dates, which gives flexibility, and the common dividend is already suspended, but the preferred dividend of USD 20.19 million a year remains. Capitalized interest fell to USD 16.9 million in nine months 2026 from USD 29.94 million as projects were completed, so more interest now reaches expense.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry limits pricing. The company competes with developers, owners and operators of similar office and studio property in the same markets, some with greater financial resources, and says it may have to give concessions, abatements and tenant improvements to renew or re-let space. Same-store rent per square foot fell while occupancy rose and leasing cost per square foot rose, so recovery is being bought with concessions, which limits how much of the NOI gain reaches free cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M24; calculation M35; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 59, 62

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of new entrants is not established. The filings give no market supply or rent data, so no credit conclusion rests on it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The threat of substitutes shows up as vacancy and as weaker production activity. The office lease expiry table shows 2,944,042 square feet of vacant space at 2026-09-30, of which 371,066 square feet was at Skyport Plaza, sold on 2026-10-15, and the Quixote stage and production business lost money in 2025 on lower production activity. Both lower the rent and service income that supports debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyer power is high for large tenants. Four tenants provide 28.6% of office rent, Google's three leases expire in 2028 and 2029, and the company states that renewals can require concessions and early termination rights; the Element LA termination fee shows tenants can also buy out leases. The Netflix leases at ICON, CUE and EPIC run to 2031 and support the collateral of the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 54–55; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 93

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Supplier power sits with lenders and with unions. Secured lenders priced the 2025 Office Portfolio loan at SOFR plus 4.15% and the 1918 Eighth loan at 6.16%, and the next refinancing will be priced in the same market, while collective bargaining disputes in the entertainment industry have halted production activity and reduced demand for studios.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two categories alter credit quality. The economic category matters most: borrowing costs reset when the swapped Hollywood Media Portfolio loan and the 2027 notes refinance, and the company's own risk statement says its growth depends on external capital outside its control, so interest rates and access to the CMBS and bond markets act directly on liquidity and refinancing capacity. The social and technological category works through tenant demand: a significant portion of rental revenue comes from technology and media and entertainment tenants, so layoffs, relocations and production slowdowns in those industries feed vacancy, concessions and studio use.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Political and regulatory factors, mainly local property taxes and entertainment labour agreements, are secondary and not quantified in the filings. Foreign exchange is minor: the Bentall Centre loan is in Canadian dollars and held in an unconsolidated venture with a company carve-out guarantee.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths for creditors are same-store leasing recovery, long-dated anchor leases with Google, the City and County of San Francisco, Netflix and Amazon, equity-funded deleveraging in 2025 with the common dividend suspended, wide balance-sheet covenant cushions, and a Hollywood loan rate fixed by swap to its maturity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M24; calculation M25; calculation M41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 54–55

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses are the concentration of 2027 maturities in two instruments, net leverage of 9.27x to 11.61x, negative free cash flow met from sales, a secured share of debt of 50.90%, and a studio segment that earns 2.98% of segment profit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M15; calculation M02; calculation M22; calculation M26; calculation M40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are an early refinancing of the Hollywood loan and the 3.95% notes before the November 2027 dates, replacement of the December 2026 revolver tranche, stabilisation of Washington 1000 by the fourth quarter of 2027, further Quixote cost cuts, and disposals of properties whose holding periods the company has shortened, such as Hill7, at values that cover their loans.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Threats that could weaken credit quality are refinancing spreads near the Office Portfolio level, failure of the covenant conditions for the Office Portfolio extensions, failures among large tenants as at Weil, further impairments that lower asset coverage, and labour disputes that stop production.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: calculation M20; calculation M19; calculation M51; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 33

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial profile is weak overall, and the evidence supports a mixed reading across the nine dimensions. Scale and market position are average: trailing revenue is USD 807.07 million from a Class-A West Coast portfolio, but the base is shrinking through sales. Competitive advantage is average, resting on anchor tenants and a vertically integrated studio platform whose profit contribution is small. Business diversification is weak, with two segments of which studio earns 2.98% of segment profit, a concentrated tenant base and a West Coast footprint. Cost and capex flexibility is weak, because commitments, leasing costs and fixed property costs absorb cash. Margin stability is average, with an EBITDA margin of 38.74% in the latest quarter held up by cost cuts against office operating deleverage. Free cash flow stability is weak, because free cash flow is negative. Ability to refinance is weak, with ratings of B2, B and B+ after downgrades in November 2024, May 2025 and June 2025, and USD 1,479.77 million due in 2027. Liquidity is average: adequate until 2027 but covering 0.42x of 2027 principal after the December 2026 expiry. Financial policy and governance are average, creditor-aligned in action, with no sponsor and no limit on debt in the organizational documents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation M45; calculation M33; calculation M40; calculation M13; calculation M22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 73; 10-K_2025-12-31_hpp-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 26

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The main supports are long-dated anchor leases, same-store leasing recovery, demonstrated equity access in 2025 and wide asset-based covenant cushions. The main constraints are leverage, thin coverage, the 2027 wall, negative free cash flow and a rising secured share. The trend is better than the level: net leverage fell from 13.55x at 2024-12-31 to 9.92x at 2025-12-31 and 9.27x on trailing EBITDA, but the fall was funded by equity and sales, not earnings growth, and the run-rate figure is 11.61x. The datapoints missing for a firmer opinion are the executed credit documents, the size of the termination fee income, the price of the tender offer, cash after the October events, and market prices and rents.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation M02; calculation M08; 10-Q_2026-09-30_hpp-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 29, 47

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every debt instrument is listed as the debt note prints it; the operating partnership issues the notes, the registrant guarantees them, and the secured loans are property-level and non-recourse apart from limited customary guarantees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Principal falls due mainly in 2027 and 2030, and the 2027 bucket is almost entirely the 3.95% notes and the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is cash plus the undrawn revolver; restricted cash and the venture loans are excluded, and one revolver tranche expires within twelve months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The smallest printed gap in proportion to its level is fixed charge cover on the revolver, 0.2x or 13.33% of the minimum, followed by total liabilities to total asset value, 15.9 pp or 26.50% of the limit. The minimum for fixed charge cover was printed as 1.4x at 2024-12-31 after the January 2025 amendment and is printed as 1.5x at 2025-12-31 and later dates; the schedule of the steps is not printed. Senior note asset coverage fell from 316.8% at 2026-06-30 to 301.5% at 2026-09-30, in the quarter that included USD 147.83 million of impairments, although the filings do not link the two. The issuer's fixed charge cover of 1.7x uses adjusted EBITDA and fixed charges as the credit agreement defines them, which differs from the 2.60x of EBITDA over cash interest paid net of capitalized interest computed here, and the filings do not reconcile the two.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The claims below sit outside total debt of USD 3,413.597 million; the recourse guarantees and the venture loans are contingent or off balance sheet, and the preferred stock ranks behind all debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The short-term outlook, over 12 to 24 months, is dominated by the refinancing and by the trailing figures rolling over. The revolver tranche of USD 333.3 million lapses on 2026-12-21 and the two November 2027 maturities approach, and the fourth quarter of 2025, whose EBITDA was USD 140.57 million, leaves the trailing window at 2026-12-31. If the fourth quarter of 2026 matches the third, EBITDA for 2026 is USD 280.52 million and net leverage on the 2026-09-30 net debt is 11.60x with cash interest cover of 2.08x, an Analyst Judgement that shows reported leverage rising by the next annual report even with no change in operations. Tailwinds are the third phase of the City and County of San Francisco lease at 1455 Market, which began in the second quarter of 2026, studio NOI that improved to USD 7.38 million in nine months 2026 from a loss of USD 10.46 million, lower general and administrative expense, and no revolver drawing until October. Headwinds are the loss of Skyport Plaza income, the PayPal lease expiry at Fourth and Traction, the Weil wind-down, the Quixote wind-down costs and the extra 2.00% a year that accrues on the Hill7 loan from 2026-11-06.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The medium-term outlook, over three to five years, turns on the 2029 and 2030 principal of USD 1,417.08 million and on the 58.4% of office rent that expires between 2028 and 2031, which is when the long anchor leases come up for renewal. Washington 1000 is expected to stabilise by the fourth quarter of 2027, which would add NOI, while the 3.3 million square feet of future development has no committed dates and would need new capital. Sector evidence beyond the company's own descriptions is not supplied, so the effect of technology and media demand, production activity and entertainment labour disputes on rents is not established; the company describes all three as risks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside scenario starts with the refinancing market for office-weighted and studio collateral staying expensive or closed as the November 2027 dates approach, while the company still relies on asset sales. The first operational break is that sales slow or the 2027 and 2028 expiries, which cover 32.3% of office rent, roll at lower occupancy or rents, so same-store NOI stops rising while sold assets have already removed income. The financial transmission runs through interest: refinancing the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan at a rate USD 16.69 million to USD 32.63 million a year higher than today's swap-fixed cost takes cash interest cover on annualised EBITDA from 2.07x to between 1.85x and 1.67x, and fixed charge cover, reported at 1.7x against a 1.5x minimum, falls by a comparable proportion of its base. If the three conditional extensions of the Office Portfolio loan were also unavailable, 2027 principal would be USD 1,721.85 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The liquidity effect is that cash plus revolver commitments of USD 622.53 million after the December expiry would meet only part of USD 1,479.77 million of 2027 principal, leaving USD 857.23 million to be refinanced, sold or raised before any further draw; the October sales of USD 84.9 million gross cover about a tenth of that. Management levers are further disposals, USD 59.2 million of at-the-market capacity, deferral of uncommitted development, and the dividend discipline already in place; the Series C preferred dividend of USD 20.19 million a year continues. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis into the first half of 2027, but it does not appear sufficient to repay the 2027 maturities without access to refinancing, so the scenario does not assume a default and treats the refinancing as the point at which default risk is decided.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Hudson Pacific presents a weak business profile supported by long-dated anchor leases, a recovering same-store portfolio and creditor-aligned policy, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 9.27x on trailing EBITDA and 11.61x on run-rate EBITDA, thin cash interest cover and negative free cash flow. Cash-flow durability appears weak due to heavy leasing costs, interest that takes 48.22% of run-rate EBITDA and income removed by sales. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Hollywood Media Portfolio loan and the 3.95% notes being refinanced before November 2027, on replacement of the December 2026 revolver tranche, and on collateral values in the studio and office assets. The primary downside path is a refinancing at higher spreads while earnings are lower after sales and lease expiries. Further analysis would require the executed credit documents, the size of the termination fee income, the price of the tender offer and cash after the October events, and market data. The strongest credit support is the combination of long-dated anchor tenants and same-store leasing recovery, the weakest material dimension is refinancing capacity against the 2027 wall, and the primary downside path is monitored through cash plus revolver against 2027 principal and through fixed charge cover. Business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data is supplied. Top risk: refinancing of the November 2027 maturities.
